title: Janus P vs NP master research checkpoint — proof-carrying algorithm, open-access evidence watch, C11/exact-channel lineage

authority.meaning: Preserves goals, verified results, open questions, execution discipline, and source-search policy. It does not promote any OPEN claim.

primary_mission.objective: Advance the P versus NP research program by constructing and verifying an exact, proof-carrying algorithmic route rather than asserting P=NP.
primary_mission.semantic_requirement: Every representation/reduction step must preserve semantics exactly and carry a reconstructable/verifiable certificate.
primary_mission.universality_requirement: Polynomiality of a subroutine, finite laboratory, restricted graph class, or diagnostic corpus is not universality.

permanent_epistemic_firewalls: proof-system lower bound != problem lower bound != general SAT lower bound
representation change is admissible only when semantics is preserved exactly
diagnostic/replay evidence != formal proof authority unless separately proved
tw(C)>k for one witness != unbounded treewidth
polynomial certification given a decomposition != polynomial discovery unless discovery itself is proved polynomial

open_access_research_policy.instruction: For each new frontier object, theorem, algorithmic primitive, obstruction, separator, coloring terminal, decomposition, invariant, or complexity claim, check open-access literature and public materials before scientific promotion.
targets: errata, theses, lecture notes, and public technical reports
purpose: find existing positive or negative results that change the frontier
bind claims to primary sources where possible
locate public artifacts needed for independent replay
separate source authority from our own diagnostics
open_access_research_policy.workflow: search/open-access audit -> source freeze -> formal statement/preregistration -> execution -> independent replay -> seal
open_access_research_policy.rule: Do not retrofit literature after promotion; source audit should precede or accompany the gate that depends on it.

experimental_chain: close execution PR without merge when that is the frozen workflow
proof_carrying_workflow.stop_rule: STOP means no automatic successor gate.
proof_carrying_workflow.successor_rule: Do not mechanically escalate separator size, treewidth, backdoor size, or repair. First inspect whether the obstruction has a new structural explanation or an already-known polynomial terminal.

exact_channel_interface: c in L, f in R

layer_1.proof_shape: maximum matching gives nu(X) internally vertex-disjoint direct paths plus hub; minimum vertex cover U gives separator {z} union U; Konig gives |U|=nu(X)

layer_2B.construction: For each deletion set S, contract each connected component of G[L-S] and G[R-S] separately plus surviving z into component-refined quotient Bhat_S.
layer_2B.transfer: If for k=nu(X), Bhat_S is connected for every |S|<=k, then kappa(G)>=k+1; the vertex-cover cut gives equality.

abstract_two_block_channel_theory.algorithmic_firewall: Theorem validity is distinct from discovery and certification complexity.

discovery.anchor_pair_characterization: (c,f) representable iff cf is a nonedge, N(c) intersection N(f)={z}, and Reach_D(R0) intersection L0 is empty
discovery.feasible_partitions: successor-closed sets R with R_min subseteq R subseteq R_max
discovery.lattice: After SCC contraction, feasible partitions are upper sets of the condensation DAG; the family is a distributive lattice under intersection/union.
discovery.fixed_pair_hub_search: none; the hub is unique if representation exists
discovery.global_clean_complexity: O(n^2(n+m)) worst-case using anchor-first search and one reachability instance per nonedge pair with singleton common neighbour

canonical_ports.P_L: {u in L : N(u) intersection R != empty}
canonical_ports.P_R: {v in R : N(v) intersection L != empty}

capacity_invariant.theorem: For every exact-channel representation of the same anchor pair, nu(X)=rho_G(c,f).
capacity_invariant.consequence: Use canonical bottom solution R_min; no lattice optimization is required for capacity.

compute maximum matching and minimum vertex cover in bipartite X
compute/certify exact global vertex connectivity kappa(G)
